A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAD research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite content relocation, renumbering, and the added checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagnostic experiments across four datasets, visual grounding and textual interpretability results, and extensive ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original diagnostic, interpretability, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The retrieval and LLM refinement procedure, guideline-enhanced contrastive loss, negative-sampling rule, and dual diagnostic decoder remain unchanged. Omitting a sampling hyperparameter value changes documentation, without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MIMIC-ICD53, Harvard-FairVLMed, SkinCAP, and NACC, plus ChestX-Det grounding and FairVLMed converted to VQA. Dataset construction, represented populations, and task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain MedFuse, BiomedCLIP, KAD, DrFuse, and HEALNet. Figure 5 retains Qwen2.5-VL-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, and Lingshu-7B; Appendix C.2 also retains its unimodal comparator sets.

E3.justification: Reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, backbone choices, and few-shot/SFT evaluation settings are retained. Removal of the explicit negative-sampling value is a documentation omission, without a replacement setting or evidence of a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Component, backbone, refinement, and knowledge-source ablations remain unchanged, as do label-wise analyses, attention cases, and hyperparameter sweeps. The existing cost analysis moves from Section 4.5 to Appendix C.7.

E5.justification: Both versions report variance and five independent runs in Table 7. The new checklist reiterates this existing practice; it introduces no new run counts, uncertainty estimation, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched tables and plots retain their results. For example, RAD's four dataset Avg scores remain 57.28, 86.63, 88.64, and 58.12 in v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1. Interpretability and appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, loss equations, interpretability definitions, and Appendix B.3 contrastive-loss derivation are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical results are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: guideline-guided RAD, dual-axis interpretability evaluation, and MIMIC-ICD53 construction. Claims of diagnostic superiority and guideline-aligned interpretability retain their scope.

C2.justification: Explanations of guideline alignment, downstream adaptability, ablation findings, and computational scalability are retained. Appendix A.2 preserves the same limitation concerning a static knowledge corpus and required updates.

D1.justification: v1 Section 4.1 explicitly sets the negative-sampling ratio to 5; v2 removes that statement while retaining the parameter in Section 3.2.2. Other implementation details and access information remain available or are repeated in the checklist; timing information is relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds Han et al., Trustworthy machine learning: From data to models, as reference 19 supporting the introduction's trustworthiness motivation. The existing 76 references and substantive related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds a NeurIPS checklist, expands affiliations and acknowledgements, reverses the textual/visual interpretability subsection order, and moves cost analysis into the appendix. The scientific narrative otherwise remains nearly identical.

P2.justification: The same 12 figures and 10 tables are retained. Tables 1 and 2 exchange numbering, Figure 3 and Table 10 are relocated, Figure 5's caption is shortened, and spacing and pagination change.

improvement.justification: The scientific claims and evidence remain stable, but v2 removes the explicit negative-sampling setting of 5 while retaining a loss that depends on it, slightly weakening reproducibility from the paper. The checklist largely repeats existing disclosures, and the added citation and editorial rearrangements do not offset this limited technical-information loss.
